# Isleta 2.6.0
The island now tells you when an update is ready, swiping always reaches your pages, and album covers keep loading however long Isleta has been running.
## New
- **The island tells you when an update is ready, starting with the next one.** Isleta's icon appears beside the notch, with a download mark, even while music plays. Open the island to read what is new, then press Install Update… to install and restart.
## Improved
- **Swiping over a call, a meeting or a volume or brightness level opens your pages.** You go to Today, then Music if something is playing, then Weather, instead of a second copy of what was already on screen. Tapping a page dot works the same way. - **Album covers that are slow to load still arrive.** A cover the player is still downloading is asked for again a few seconds later, rather than leaving the placeholder for the whole song.
## Fixed
- **Album covers no longer stop appearing after Isleta has run for days.** One stalled request could stop every later cover, and the audio quality badge, from loading until Isleta was relaunched. - **A city you type is used for the weather.** If location access had been reset, the island kept waiting for your location and said "Weather not available right now" instead of using the city. - **Typing a city asks for its weather once you stop typing**, rather than once for every letter.
## Requirements
macOS 26 or later, on Apple Silicon. Displays with a real notch get the island; a Mac without one gets a floating island on the main display.
## Known limitations
- **The lean at the end of a range needs Accessibility.** Reaching the end of the volume or brightness no longer moves the island on its own, and the press after it is only visible to Isleta with that permission granted. The reading itself, and the bar filling and emptying, work either way. - **A muted Mac's bar cannot be dragged.** It is drawn at nothing whatever the volume behind it is, so pressing it opens the island instead. Unmute first. - **You cannot see who is calling.** macOS does not let apps outside Apple read that, or answer for you. Isleta shows that a call is happening and nothing more. - **Weather needs your location, or a city you type.** Isleta asks for neither until you use it. - **A connected device's battery is read once, when it connects.** It does not tick down as you wear them, and most non-Apple headphones report no level at all. - **A timer started by Siri, Shortcuts or Control Center can take a few seconds to appear.** One started by hand in Clock is there immediately. - **Replacing the system HUDs is on by default, and it needs Accessibility.** Two switches in Settings hand the keys back. Quitting Isleta hands them back too; if Isleta is force-quit, the system HUD stays out of the way until Isleta next starts. Brightness covers the built-in display only. - **Apple's own banner still appears when headphones connect.** It is drawn by the menu bar rather than by the HUD helper Isleta can stand in for, so the island announces the connection alongside it rather than instead of it. - **The island sits above Mission Control.** In a real notch it covers nothing; a floating island can sit over the middle of the space labels. - **Today and tomorrow show five entries and then a count.** A busy pair of days says how many it could not fit rather than scrolling. - **Swiping away from a meeting hides its Join button until the island next opens.** The meeting stays in the island's edges, and the button is back the next time you open it. - **The equalizer moves in a set pattern rather than to the song.** Its colors come from the cover; its motion does not come from the audio.

# Isleta 2.5.1
The island no longer goes missing after you unlock your Mac.
## Fixed
- **The island comes back after every unlock.** Unlocking quickly, before the screen dimmed, could leave the notch empty and unclickable until Isleta was quit and reopened. Pointing at the notch now also brings it back if it is ever left behind.

# Isleta 2.5.0
The weather page is in color. Each day's range is drawn in the colors of its temperatures, the way Weather does, so a hot week reads warm and a cold one reads blue at a glance. The bars beside the music now flow smoothly between the cover's colors.
## Improved
- **The forecast's bars are colored by temperature.** Blue when it is freezing, green when it is mild, yellow into orange and red as it gets hot, so the colors show what the week is like. - **Today's bar marks the temperature right now.** A white dot sits on today's range where the current reading falls. - **The weather icons are in full color, and the chance of rain is in blue.** Suns are yellow and raindrops blue, so a wet day stands out down the list before you read a number.
## Fixed
- **The bars beside the music flow from one color to the next.** They still run from the left of the cover to the right, as one smooth blend instead of six unrelated colors side by side.
